holding_summary: In a fire-insurance dispute, the referee found that the risk on the insured dwelling was not increased by the fact that the household kept an average of ten boarders (men working for the occupant on a court-house construction job) rather than a formal commercial boarding house. The General Term declined to disturb that finding on appeal. The case does not otherwise classify the legal character (lease/license/lodging) of the boarding arrangement.

quotes.text: did not keep it as a general boarding house; only boarded men at work for Welch; they had some boarders the night of the fire; upon an average had ten boarders.
